answers.explanation: Scaling up (vertical) is simple, but big machines cost disproportionately more and there's a ceiling.
Scaling out uses shared-nothing machines that coordinate only over the network.
Stateless services just need more copies behind a load balancer. Data has to be replicated, partitioned, and kept consistent, which is most of this course.
Elasticity helps with unpredictable load, at the cost of more moving parts.
Operability is about making life easy for the people who keep the system running.
Simplicity means managing complexity, and abstractions are how you hide it.
Most of the cost comes after launch: fixing bugs, keeping it running, and adapting it to new needs.
